title: POC Hosting Prioritization Radar and Action Runbook
content:
Purpose:
This note is a compact, actionable playbook for Solutions Engineering (SE) when running customer POCs that must choose between Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments. It combines a quick prioritization heuristic (radar), a short risk breakdown, and an executable runbook (checklist + timeline). Aim: reduce meetings and accelerate an agreed hosting plan within the first 5 working days of a POC kickoff.

Audience:
- SE engagement lead
- Customer engineering contact
- PM / Solutions architect supporting the opportunity
- Delivery SRE (when dedicated/private likely)

Scope and assumptions:
- Covers initial choice for POC environment and immediate mitigations for top-5 risks.
- Not a full legal review or procurement doc. For enterprise contracts, loop in Legal/CS early.
- Assumes Redwood models in our catalog; if customer requires third-party model binaries, escalate to infra/model-onboarding.

1) Quick prioritization radar (how to use)
- Within kickoff, run through 6 compact signals. Score as High / Medium / Low urgency. The highest-urgency signals guide hosting choice.
  Signals: data-sensitivity, latency requirement, sustained throughput, regional sovereignty, integration barrier (networking/VPN), SLAs / uptime / audit needs.

2) Heuristic mapping (one-line rule)
- If data-sensitivity == High OR regional sovereignty == Required -> Private
- Else if sustained throughput > 100 qps or predictable committed spend needed -> Dedicated
- Else (short test, exploratory, low integration friction) -> Hosted

3) Risk radar (top failure modes and mitigations)
- Data exfil / compliance (High risk for Hosted). Mitigation: sign NDA immediately; recommend Private or Dedicated with customer-managed VPC when legal requires. Engage security-ops and customer security review within 48 hours.
- Latency spikes during scale (Moderate). Mitigation: baseline perf test in first 48 hours, enable autoscaling policy on Dedicated or use regional Hosted endpoints for lower RTT.
- Cost blowouts on long token/embedding jobs (Moderate). Mitigation: set strict hard caps/quotas, token limits, and use Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching + quantization).
- Integration (networking) delays (High). Mitigation: early network test (curl/tracepath), VPN checklist; if VPN/peering likely to slow schedule by >5 business days, consider hybrid approach: Hosted for control-plane + Private/Dedicated for inference plane.
- Observability blind spots (Low-Medium). Mitigation: attach console dashboards and sampling traces in first 72 hours; map SLOs.

4) Actionable runbook (day-by-day, first 10 business days)
- Day 0 (pre-kick): share this doc + simple intake form with customer (one pager): expected qps, sample sequences, data-sensitivity, region, compliance needs.
- Day 1 (kickoff): collect intake, run prioritization radar live (10–15 min). Decide provisional hosting path (Hosted / Dedicated / Private). Raise JIRA SE-XXXX.
- Day 2: run network connectivity smoke (customer network, firewall rules, NAT, peering). If firewall blocks outbound to Hosted endpoints, flag.
- Day 3: baseline perf test with representative payloads (50/100/500 tokens) and capture latencies and token/second. Document in SE JIRA.
- Day 4: security quick-check: data flow diagram + storage/retention note. If High sensitivity, start Private onboarding checklist.
- Day 5–7: if Dedicated/Private chosen, provision minimal capacity and run acceptance test; if Hosted chosen, enable quotas and test failover to a fallback model variant.
- Day 8–10: collect metrics, tune batching/kv-cache settings, propose final hosting for POC run. Prepare customer-facing runbook for ops handover.

5) Checklist fragments (copyable)
- Networking: required outbound endpoints, recommended ports, IP allowlist, expected egress patterns.
- Security: data residency statement, encryption at rest/in transit status, KMS needs, audit log hooks.
- Observability: sampling rate, key dashboards (latency, token cost, error rate), log retention request.
- Cost controls: per-key quotas, max tokens/day, abort thresholds, alerting to SE channel.
- Fallbacks: model variant mapping (e.g., prefer quantized variant with identical facade for cost-sensitive fallback).

6) Hybrid option pattern (practical when customer is blocked on one signal)
- Use case: customer requires low-latency inference in-region but cannot approve Private in time.
- Pattern: Put inference in Dedicated pool in the customer region (or Dedicated via colo), keep control-plane and evaluation on Hosted. Provide strict token quotas and run a temp audit of logs. Document network egress and data flow.

7) Example customer archetypes and recommended starter plan (fast reference)
- Regulated fintech (PII + audit): Private deployment (VPC) + 2-week security review; early Legal / CS engagement.
- High-throughput consumer chat (500+ qps): Dedicated with autoscaling policy; pre-warm and run sustained throughput test.
- Product prototype (early, low users): Hosted with strict quotas and sampling enabled; quick switch plan to Dedicated if usage rises.

8) Escalation matrix (who to call)
- Security / Compliance: Priya Desai (secops) and Legal@redwood (customer contracts).
- Infra provisioning (Dedicated/Private): Jonah Reyes (infra lead).
- Observability / Console: Liam O'Connor (product/console).
- Exec / Pricing exceptions: Solutions Eng director (cc: growth-sales).

9) Customer communications templates (short snippets)
- Hosted suggestion: "We recommend starting on Redwood Hosted to reduce setup time. We'll set strict quotas and monitor token usage; if we see sustained traffic, we can convert to Dedicated within days."
- Private suggestion: "Given your regulatory needs, we recommend the Private deployment path. We'll start the VPC onboarding checklist immediately; expect ~3–4 weeks for full on-prem/VPC readiness depending on approvals."

10) Open questions / TODOs (for SE team)
- TODO: create a single-playbook automation template in Confluence to auto-fill the intake and generate a provisioning JIRA. (owner: Arielle)
- Q: SLA addendum template — where is canonical pricing + SLA doc for Dedicated? (owner: Jonah)
- TODO: add a short perf script repo link for 1-click baseline runs (owner: Liam).

Appendix A — Minimal intake form (copy/paste):
- Expected average qps:
- Peak qps:

- Data sensitivity: (Low / Medium / High)
- Country/region data must reside in:
- Required start date for POC:
- Primary contact (name + email):

Appendix B — Quick links:
- Confluence: SE/POC-hosting-playbook
- Perf repo: github.com/redwood-inference/se-perf-scripts (WIP)
- JIRA template: SE-1248 (provisioning template)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc short; customers appreciate a one-paragraph recommendation + 1–2 actionable next steps.
- We should build a small UI in Console to stub intake -> provisional hosting recommendation. Low-hanging automation win.
